note: Review candidate only; not for import as an active exam until the 12-page PDF is academically approved, published to learning_materials, and item-level reviewer signoffs are complete.

questions.stem: What is the central responsibility of a journalist in this course?
options: Repeat every quote from an official source
Produce the fastest possible viral headline
Find, verify, contextualize and communicate information accurately
Publish only stories that attract sponsorship
questions.rationale: The learning route centers on independently tested public-interest reporting Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: Why is polished writing insufficient to establish an accurate report?
options: Readers can verify prose by its length
A good headline proves the facts beneath it
Grammar can replace corroboration
Persuasive language does not verify the underlying claims
questions.rationale: Verification depends on evidence rather than presentation Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: Which skill is an explicit learning outcome of the journalism manual?
options: Maximize posting frequency regardless of accuracy
Replace interviewing with artificial quotations
Allow advertisements to control editorial judgments
Distinguish allegation, interpretation and verified observation
questions.rationale: The learning outcomes distinguish kinds of claims and require verification Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: What should a working story proposition make possible?
options: A guarantee of favorable public reaction
An automatic exemption from source checking
A test of whether the key claim is supported
A promise that all witnesses agree
questions.rationale: A testable proposition helps identify what evidence is needed Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: Which example describes reporting rather than mere repetition?
options: Publishing a viral repost because it is popular
Copying a public-relations statement unchanged
Checking an announcement against dated original records
Treating one rumor as a confirmed event
questions.rationale: The core method independently examines evidence behind a statement Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: What should reporters do when material facts remain unknown?
options: Invent a plausible explanation for readers
Remove every attribution from the story
Describe the unknown claim as certain
Explain relevant uncertainty and continue checking
questions.rationale: The course emphasizes transparent uncertainty Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: What public benefit should a report be assessed against?
options: Whether the article contains many dramatic adjectives
Whether a sponsor prefers the headline
Whether the author has a large following
Whether readers gain relevant and dependable information
questions.rationale: Journalism is evaluated against usefulness and accuracy Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: How is a fictional case properly used in training?
options: As a labeled simulation, never as a real reported event
As an anonymous eyewitness account
As an unpublished interview with a real source
As a documentary photograph of current events
questions.rationale: The manual explicitly labels practice scenarios fictional Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: What should a reporting workflow preserve?
options: Only the final draft without any notes
Only the headline chosen before research
An auditable path from evidence to published claims
Only anonymous comments from social media
questions.rationale: An audit trail supports corrections and evidence checks Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: What follows from a self-assessment of a reading exercise?
options: It guides study but does not automatically award certification
It always replaces the official final examination
It proves the learner met all assessment standards
It authorizes the student to issue a certificate
questions.rationale: Self-study completion and official certification are distinct Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 2.

questions.stem: What makes an issue potentially newsworthy?
options: The loudness of a social-media argument alone
The length of a promotional message
Verified impact and relevance to the public
A sensational image without provenance
questions.rationale: Public value rather than spectacle drives story selection Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: Which question is the strongest starting point for a service-delay story?
options: What was scheduled, what occurred and whom did it affect?
Who deserves blame before any facts are checked?
How can the story appear more dramatic?
Which version will generate the most angry comments?
questions.rationale: Testable event and impact questions guide reporting Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: A company announces 200 future jobs. Which headline is unsupported without more data?
options: The company announced a plan involving 200 jobs
The company has already hired 200 employees
The announcement concerns possible new positions
The company described its employment intentions
questions.rationale: An announced plan is not proof of completed hiring Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: Why should a story brief include the people affected?
options: It guarantees that the story has no ethical concerns
It makes verification unnecessary
It determines the final headline before facts are collected
It clarifies who may benefit from reliable reporting
questions.rationale: A public-interest question needs a defined audience Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: What is the danger of deciding the headline before checking evidence?
options: The source log becomes too short
The reporter may favor facts that support a predetermined angle
Every headline becomes too formal
The article will necessarily lack a quotation
questions.rationale: Premature framing can distort selection and interpretation Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: How should an emotionally forceful allegation be handled?
options: Publish it as fact if the language is confident
Assume the witness saw everything described
Separate the act of making the claim from evidence that it is true
Use an anonymous headline to avoid any checking
questions.rationale: Statements do not establish their own truth Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: Which source would best clarify whether advertised jobs were actually filled?
options: Employment records or a verified hiring count
The size of the company's billboard
The number of times the announcement was shared
An unrelated historic marketing campaign
questions.rationale: Completed hiring requires evidence of filled positions Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: What does editorial independence mean in selecting stories?
options: A sponsor cannot purchase or secretly control factual conclusions
Advertisements determine which allegations are true
A subject can veto any critical evidence
Only profitable events merit publication
questions.rationale: Editorial judgment must not be controlled by commercial interests Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: Why should a reporting brief list unresolved facts?
options: To make every draft longer
To prevent unsupported details being presented as established
To discourage further reporting
To replace the need to contact relevant sources
questions.rationale: Uncertainty notes identify reporting limits Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: When may the planned story angle need to change?
options: When a more sensational adjective is available
When a sponsor requests a stronger accusation
When verified records contradict the initial proposition
Whenever a post gains more likes
questions.rationale: The angle should follow evidence, not the reverse Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 3.

questions.stem: What does firsthand knowledge establish most directly?
options: The cause of every event across the region
The accuracy of every official database
What a source personally observed or experienced
The future outcome of a disputed policy
questions.rationale: Source competence is claim-specific Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: Why are two news accounts repeating one social post not independent corroboration?
options: Both may depend on a single unverified origin
They were published on separate sites
Their headlines use different words
They appeared at different hours
questions.rationale: Independence concerns the underlying evidence chain Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: What should a source log record?
options: Only the reporter's preferred headline
Only page views and audience likes
Only the source's occupation
Claim, source, date, attribution terms and verification status
questions.rationale: A source log preserves how each assertion was checked Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: What is the limitation of a dated official announcement?
options: No official announcements can be cited
It may prove what was announced but not that the action occurred
Every announced action is already complete
It cannot contain dates or names
questions.rationale: Documents establish their contents within a defined scope Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: How should a journalist handle a source speaking outside their area of expertise?
options: Accept all technical interpretations from the source
Assess the specific claim rather than assume universal authority
Avoid all interviews with specialists
Describe the source as a firsthand witness to everything
questions.rationale: Authority and direct knowledge have boundaries Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: Why must a reporter verify whether photograph and closure notice describe the same event?
options: Their times and locations might not match
All authentic photographs have current timestamps
A notice always covers every road in the city
Photos prove an event's cause without context
questions.rationale: Related evidence must match the claimed event Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: When should a serious allegation seek independent confirmation?
options: Only if the reporter disagrees with the source
Only after a final correction is requested
Never when a source holds public office
When practicable, before publishing as an established fact
questions.rationale: Serious factual allegations need proportionate corroboration Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: What is a useful distinction between a direct witness and an institutional spokesperson?
options: Both must have identical knowledge of causes
Both automatically prove every disputed detail
Neither can provide meaningful evidence
One can report experience while the other may state an institutional position
questions.rationale: Different source roles support different claims Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: How should a quote from an interview be treated?
options: Invent concise wording that sounds plausible
Preserve the speaker's actual words and relevant context
Combine two people into one attributed quotation
Remove qualifying language that changes its meaning
questions.rationale: Quotation accuracy requires fidelity to actual speech Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: Which condition should be agreed before a sensitive interview?
options: How many social reactions the story must receive
The permitted attribution or confidentiality arrangement
Which headline the source prefers
Whether all future editor questions are forbidden
questions.rationale: Attribution conditions should be clear in advance Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 4.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a reporting plan from a broad topic idea?
options: A list of likely advertising customers
A set of dramatic adjectives
A headline that assumes the conclusion
Specific evidence tasks, sources and outstanding questions
questions.rationale: A reporting plan tells the journalist how to test claims Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: Why seek evidence that could challenge the original theory?
options: To reduce confirmation bias and test alternative explanations
To create artificial balance between facts and rumors
To guarantee the story is favorable to every person
To prevent any editorial conclusion
questions.rationale: Fair inquiry tests disconfirming evidence Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: What should direct field notes separate?
options: Past dates from future dates only
Public statements from all documentary evidence
Observed details from what other people claimed
Reporter preferences from their own style notes
questions.rationale: Observation and testimony require distinct attribution Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: A reporter sees barriers but does not know why they were installed. What is defensible?
options: State that corruption caused the closure
Identify the responsible contractor without records
Claim an official safety order exists
Describe the observed barriers and seek the cause from relevant evidence
questions.rationale: Observed objects do not establish their cause Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: What is fair response practice for a serious allegation against an organization?
options: Allow the subject to delete the reporter's notes
Publish without considering a reply under all circumstances
Treat a denial as equal proof regardless of documents
Offer a relevant opportunity to address the material claim when feasible
questions.rationale: Fair response and proportional evidence are compatible Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: Why should a reporter document when a field event was observed?
options: The date and time affect whether the report fits the claimed event
Every observation is timeless
Time records replace the need for sources
All public services operate on the same schedule
questions.rationale: Temporal context is needed to validate observations Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: How should original interview recordings be handled for verification?
options: Retain them appropriately so edits and quotes can be checked
Delete them immediately after a rough transcript
Modify the source's voice to sound more confident
Keep only excerpts that favor the proposed headline
questions.rationale: Original records support quote accuracy and accountability Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: Why can excessive disclosure of a witness's address be harmful?
options: It always increases factual accuracy
It may expose private information without a corresponding public benefit
An address proves that all allegations are true
Privacy concerns disappear for witnesses
questions.rationale: Publication should consider necessity and risk Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: Which verification task belongs in an exit-from-scene checklist?
options: Choose a more exciting background photograph
Confirm names, dates, locations and outstanding questions
Increase the length of the title
Find a sponsor for the story before asking questions
questions.rationale: Reporting checklists reduce avoidable factual gaps Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: What should a reporter do with a missing relevant perspective?
options: Invent a quotation representing that group
Contact an appropriate source or disclose meaningful limits
Assume one witness speaks for everyone
Ignore the absence because the draft is polished
questions.rationale: Fair coverage acknowledges material evidence gaps Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 5.

questions.stem: What must be checked before relying on a policy document?
options: Only the document's font
Issuer, version, date, status and possible amendments
Only the number of pages
Only the author's social-media followers
questions.rationale: Authenticity and current status matter Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: Why can a draft document not be reported as an enacted decision?
options: Its status does not demonstrate formal adoption
Every draft is legally binding
The document cannot contain recommendations
Drafts are never relevant to reporting
questions.rationale: Document type determines what it proves Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: What is required before comparing two percentages?
options: Only matching colors on charts
Identical title lengths
Two sources with the same logo
Compatible denominators, periods and definitions
questions.rationale: Ratios with different bases are not automatically comparable Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: A program serves 45 of 60 eligible applicants. What percentage is served?
questions.rationale: 45 divided by 60 equals 0.75 or 75 percent Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: Why can a screenshot of a public table be insufficient?
options: It may omit revisions, headers or other explanatory context
All screenshots are fabricated
A screenshot cannot contain numbers
Only images from social media can be cited
questions.rationale: Primary data and context should be checked Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: Which description correctly handles correlation?
options: It proves one event caused the other
It can be used without checking a time period
It removes the possibility of other explanations
It suggests an association that needs causal investigation
questions.rationale: Correlation alone does not establish cause Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: Why should a numerical news report state units?
options: The meaning of a figure depends on what was counted or measured
Units can always be guessed by readers
A number is self-explanatory in every context
The unit only matters in financial reporting
questions.rationale: Units are essential to interpreting figures Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: What should the reporter do when the claimed total does not reconcile with source rows?
options: Choose whichever total appears larger
Adjust missing data to match the headline
Investigate and explain the discrepancy or omit the unsupported figure
Attribute the arithmetic error to an unnamed critic
questions.rationale: Unreconciled figures are not reliable reporting Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: What should be checked before labeling a photo as taken today?
options: Only whether the image is clear
Original provenance, timestamp, location and context
Only whether the image has many shares
Only whether it depicts a familiar building
questions.rationale: An authentic picture can have a false time or place label Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: What is the value of preserving the original spreadsheet or document?
options: It guarantees every formula is correct
It makes source attribution unnecessary
It enables later verification of transformations and claims
It authorizes publication of private personal data
questions.rationale: An auditable source record supports fact-checking Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 6.

questions.stem: Which opening interview prompt is most neutral?
options: Can you describe what happened and when?
Why did you intentionally fail the community?
Who should be blamed before we review records?
How did you manage to conceal the truth?
questions.rationale: Neutral questions invite an account without assuming guilt Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: Why should a journalist prepare background research before an interview?
options: To focus questions on verified context and important gaps
To prevent the source from disagreeing
To memorize a preferred quotation
To eliminate all follow-up questions
questions.rationale: Preparation improves precision without closing inquiry Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: What makes a question leading?
options: It assumes or suggests the answer the reporter wants
It asks a source for a date
It requests a document
It asks someone to explain their role
questions.rationale: Leading wording embeds a preferred conclusion Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: A source gives an estimated figure. What is the right follow-up?
options: Replace it with an exact-looking number
Ask for its basis and whether a record can verify it
Treat the estimate as audited fact
Remove the word estimated from the draft
questions.rationale: Source reasoning and records are needed for numerical claims Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: Why should attribution terms be clarified before recording an interview?
options: To require the source to endorse the final story
To understand how information may legitimately be used
To guarantee all answers are on the record regardless of agreement
To allow fabricated anonymous quotes
questions.rationale: Consent and attribution conditions affect publication Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: What is a defensible response to an interview refusal?
options: Record the request and refusal accurately
Invent the explanation the source probably would give
Describe silence as an admission of wrongdoing
Remove every reference to the original allegation
questions.rationale: Refusal should not be transformed into invented evidence Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: How should an interviewer treat someone describing distressing events?
options: Pressure repeated testimony for dramatic effect
Demand immediate disclosure of private details
Respect safety, informed communication and appropriate breaks
Treat vulnerability as permission to bypass consent rules
questions.rationale: Sensitive interviews require additional ethical care Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: Why should precise names and terminology be confirmed after an interview?
options: Every interview includes no technical vocabulary
Names never matter to readers
A transcription mistake can materially alter a factual claim
AI transcription is always flawless
questions.rationale: Small wording errors may change identity or meaning Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: What must a reporter do before attributing an AI transcript's words as a direct quote?
options: Compare relevant portions against the original recording
Trust the transcription tool without review
Make the quote more fluent than the source
Delete the original audio
questions.rationale: Transcription tools can mishear or invent content Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: What is a good follow-up when a source alleges a policy breach?
options: Which policy provision and document supports your statement?
Should we publish your accusation immediately?
Can we describe the breach as already proven?
Who else do you think we should blame?
questions.rationale: Specific source and record questions support verification Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 7.

questions.stem: What belongs in a straight-news lead?
options: A complete history before the current event
The most consequential verified development
A dramatic conclusion unsupported by evidence
A sponsor's preferred selling message
questions.rationale: A lead should communicate the principal verified change Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: What does the inverted-pyramid structure prioritize?
options: Unverified speculation at the beginning
The least relevant background first
Essential facts before supporting context and detail
A surprise accusation without attribution at the end
questions.rationale: The structure lets readers obtain critical information early Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: What should happen if the cause of an event is unknown?
options: Invent a likely cause to satisfy every question
Attribute the cause to the most quoted person automatically
Report verified events and clearly state meaningful uncertainty
Omit all context about the event
questions.rationale: Uncertainty is preferable to invented causal explanation Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: Why is a headline subject to the same fact-checking as the article?
options: It is only decorative and cannot mislead
It is exempt if the story contains correct details
Its wording itself asserts claims readers may rely on
Only the graphic design needs inspection
questions.rationale: Headlines are factual editorial statements Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: How should a proposed action be described in a headline?
options: As completed after any announcement
As proposed or planned until adoption is established
As a verified success before implementation
As already paid for without records
questions.rationale: Status words must track actual evidence Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: Which attribution correctly describes a source's unverified prediction?
options: The spokesperson predicted that the service would expand
Records prove that expansion has been completed
The reporter observed the future expansion
The city has expanded all services
questions.rationale: Predictions must not be converted into completed facts Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: Why should a paragraph avoid mixing several unrelated assertions?
options: Single, contextualized ideas improve clarity and fact-checking
Long paragraphs automatically improve accuracy
One paragraph can substitute for all source checks
The reader should infer unstated context
questions.rationale: Focused structure improves comprehension and traceability Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: What is wrong with changing a quotation's meaning through editing?
options: It is always necessary for word limits
It misrepresents the source despite preserving some words
It becomes acceptable when the headline is longer
It is harmless if the reporter agrees with the message
questions.rationale: Accurate attribution preserves material context Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: Which link should be considered for an evidence-based public notice story?
options: A random unrelated commercial homepage
An anonymous repost with no verification
The relevant primary record when lawful and safe to share
A page that reveals unnecessary private identifiers
questions.rationale: Primary documentation can help readers inspect evidence Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: How should an article end when important details remain unverified?
options: Invent a decisive quotation for narrative impact
Declare an unsupported cause to finish strongly
Omit all reference to open questions
State the known status and practical next checks, without sensational invention
questions.rationale: The ending should not distort the evidence Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 8.

questions.stem: Why can an article be misleading even when its individual statements are true?
options: A true statement can never be used misleadingly
Only arithmetic mistakes affect accuracy
Short articles are always unethical
Selective omission can create a false overall impression
questions.rationale: Editorial review considers the whole presentation Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: What should be verified during prepublication editing?
options: Names, quotations, dates, figures and the headline's support
Only the background theme color
Only whether the headline is exciting
Only the author's publication history
questions.rationale: Accuracy review covers substantive assertions and presentation Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: What is fair handling of a documented fact and an unsupported denial?
options: Give identical weight regardless of evidence
Discard all original records to appear neutral
Assume the denial disproves the document
Describe the evidence accurately without giving false equivalence
questions.rationale: Fairness does not require false balance Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: What is the right response to a significant published factual mistake?
options: Silent replacement without any note
Leave it unchanged if it received many views
Prompt correction with a visible account of what changed
Remove all article references while denying an error
questions.rationale: Transparent corrections support accountability Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: Why must publication of private details be justified?
options: Privacy never matters to journalists
Every available address has equal public value
True personal details can be published without any editorial judgment
Even accurate disclosure can produce needless foreseeable harm
questions.rationale: Public-interest value and harm should be weighed Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: How should a fictional correction for 24 versus 14 permits be expressed?
options: Describe both values as equally correct
Quietly replace only the headline
Clearly identify the wrong figure and verified replacement
State that statistics are inherently subjective
questions.rationale: A correction should specify the error and the corrected fact Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: What is the danger of mixing a paid promotional message into an unlabeled article?
options: Paid content automatically has higher factual reliability
Readers may mistake commercial influence for independent reporting
Editorial labels are irrelevant to audience understanding
Sponsors are responsible for independent verification
questions.rationale: Transparency about commercial relationships is necessary Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: When should a newsroom seek additional qualified review?
options: Before publishing serious legal, privacy or safety-sensitive claims
Only when a headline has spelling mistakes
Whenever a source is famous regardless of risk
Never when a public-interest argument exists
questions.rationale: Material harm risk may warrant specialist review Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: What is wrong with presenting generated faces as photographs of actual witnesses?
options: It is only a minor design change
It is automatically acceptable if the image is attractive
It fabricates documentary evidence and misleads readers
It improves evidence quality without disclosure
questions.rationale: Synthetic imagery must not masquerade as genuine reportage Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: What should an editor do if the headline overstates the verified conclusion?
options: Keep it to increase reach
Add an unrelated caution at the end only
Assume readers will ignore the headline
Revise it to match the evidence before publication
questions.rationale: The strongest published claim must remain supported Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 9.

questions.stem: Does a short social caption reduce the need to verify its central claim?
options: Yes, because social audiences expect uncertainty
Only video needs verification
No, abbreviated formats require factual accuracy too
Verification applies only to print media
questions.rationale: Format length does not lower journalistic standards Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: What is a key check for a viral video with unclear origin?
options: Number of emojis in comments
Only the uploader's follower count
Original recording, date, place and uncut context
How emotionally engaging the clip appears
questions.rationale: Video context and provenance are essential Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: Why may an authentic old image mislead in a current story?
options: Authentic images always depict the current news
Old images cannot be visually accurate
Only synthetic images can be misleading
Its description may wrongly assign it to a new event
questions.rationale: Correct media can become false evidence through miscaptioning Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: What must be done after AI-assisted transcription?
options: Publish every generated word as direct speech
Verify significant names, numbers and quotations against source audio
Delete the original recording
Ask the tool to invent missing phrases
questions.rationale: AI assistance does not replace source checks Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: How should reporting and sponsorship appear to readers?
options: Intermixed without explanation
Clearly distinguished and labeled
Identified only in an internal billing system
Presented identically if the sponsor is well known
questions.rationale: Editorial independence requires transparent labeling Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: Why are accessible captions and descriptive text relevant?
options: They substitute for source verification
They prove all video claims
They are useful only for advertisements
They help diverse audiences understand verified information
questions.rationale: Accessibility is part of communicating accurate information Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: How should a journalist use audience engagement data?
options: As proof a disputed claim is true
As reception feedback without letting clicks alone define public value
As a reason to remove all verification steps
As the only selection criterion for reports
questions.rationale: Popularity is not a reliable truth test Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: What is an appropriate use of an AI summarization tool?
options: Generating invented witnesses for a missing interview
Drafting a summary that a journalist checks against the originals
Changing numbers to match a preferred headline
Publishing fabricated quotations without review
questions.rationale: AI may assist organization but cannot invent evidence Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: When should a social post preserve the word estimated?
options: Only when the number is low
Never because short captions must be categorical
Only when the source requests dramatic wording
When the underlying quantity remains an estimate
questions.rationale: Short form must retain material uncertainty Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: What should be done before publishing a clip that appears to show a disaster?
options: Treat high view counts as authentication
Use the most alarming caption available
Verify location, time, original footage and independent evidence
Assume the event is current if the clip is clear
questions.rationale: Viral distribution does not establish a clip's event context Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 10.

questions.stem: What is established by the fictional city's water-distribution notice?
options: That the entire water network is contaminated
That the city announced two temporary distribution points
That every neighborhood has lost service
That the investigation has already identified the cause
questions.rationale: The notice supports the announcement but not the viral health claim Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.

questions.stem: How should the resident's contamination assertion be classified initially?
options: An unverified claim requiring relevant confirmation
A proven public-health determination
A verified laboratory measurement
An official notice from the authority
questions.rationale: The exercise does not include evidence confirming contamination Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.

questions.stem: What source is most relevant for checking whether a health advisory exists?
options: The number of social likes
An unrelated retail advertisement
The responsible public-health authority
A resident's speculation alone
questions.rationale: Public-health guidance should be checked with the competent authority Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.

questions.stem: What details should be extracted from the original notice?
options: Issuing agency, date, distribution points, hours and contact information
Only the logo's color
Only how many people reposted it
Only nearby shops not mentioned
questions.rationale: Documented public-service details should be recorded precisely Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.

questions.stem: Why should the journalist contact the water utility?
options: To ask it to endorse a rumor
To obtain a sensational accusation
To guarantee an exact repair date without records
To check the cause, affected areas and restoration information
questions.rationale: The utility may establish operational status and limitations Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.

questions.stem: Which lead is supported by the fictional facts?
options: The city admitted citywide contamination
The city's entire network was permanently shut
The city's water system was declared toxic by laboratory tests
The city announced two temporary bottled-water distribution points while checking pressure complaints
questions.rationale: Only the temporary announcement and pressure investigation appear in the case Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.

questions.stem: What must a correction address if a distribution address was misstated?
options: Only an unrelated word choice
Only the reporter's opinion of the city
The inaccurate location and its verified replacement
Only the article's graphic style
questions.rationale: A wrong service address is a material actionable error Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.

questions.stem: Why include unresolved questions in the public-service update?
options: It allows every rumor to be repeated as fact
Readers need to distinguish confirmed instructions from remaining uncertainty
It replaces contacting appropriate authorities
It makes evidence checking optional
questions.rationale: The simulation stresses practical information and honest limits Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.

questions.stem: When can the story report a new health warning as confirmed?
options: When a resident repeats the rumor a second time
After a post reaches a popularity threshold
Whenever public concern is high
After independently verifying an actual relevant advisory
questions.rationale: A new health warning needs corresponding evidence Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the claim-and-source matrix in the exercise?
options: To assign dramatic language to every source
To map each proposed statement to evidence or an open question
To guarantee all claims are fully proven before investigation
To remove the need for a written news update
questions.rationale: The matrix makes the reporting reasoning inspectable Source: MAIC Diploma in Journalism course manual, page 11.
